samples.summary: Scope creep beyond issue #728: OOXML enum hardening and backend block-style rewrite are unrelated to the color-reset outcome
samples.evidence: The issue (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md) is scoped to "reset the text color → text is uncolored", with a plan covering the toolbar reset, the renderer `''` guard, and color normalization at the DOCX/PPTX sinks. This diff additionally rewrites `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`ALGN`/`UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` as prototype-chain-safe `Map`s, adds `listLevelAttr` clamping in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts, and rewrites `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts (partial styles, NaN guards) plus a backend controller test — none of which touch colors or appear in the task plan. samples.summary: Block-style serializer is duplicated backend/frontend; only the backend copy was hardened, so the two CRDT encoders now diverge
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` were changed to emit only present/finite fields and to ignore non-finite attributes, but the near-identical copy in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-227 still does `alignment: style.alignment` / `String(style.lineHeight)` unconditionally and `Number(attrs.x)` without a finite check. Both write and read the same Yorkie Tree, so the same document is now encoded/decoded by two different rule sets — the repo's reuse expectation would put this logic in one shared module instead.

samples.summary: Backend Tree block-style attributes may now be absent, contradicting the collaboration design doc which lists them as carried attributes
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:77-79 states `<block>` attributes carry `alignment`, `lineHeight`, `marginTop`, `marginBottom`, `textIndent`, `marginLeft`. After this change the backend writer omits any field that is absent or non-finite, and the reader falls back to `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`. That serialization-contract change is not recorded in any design doc (the diff updates docs-tables.md, docs-docx-import-export.md and slides-pptx-export.md only).

finding.summary: Scope creep beyond issue #728: OOXML enum hardening and backend block-style rewrite are unrelated to the color-reset outcome
finding.evidence: The issue (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md) is scoped to "reset the text color → text is uncolored", with a plan covering the toolbar reset, the renderer `''` guard, and color normalization at the DOCX/PPTX sinks. This diff additionally rewrites `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`ALGN`/`UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` as prototype-chain-safe `Map`s, adds `listLevelAttr` clamping in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts, and rewrites `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts (partial styles, NaN guards) plus a backend controller test — none of which touch colors or appear in the task plan. Unrequested scope in three more packages makes the fix harder to review and revert independently.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists (docx-style-map.ts:118 Map, pptx/text.ts:69/82/253, docs-tree.ts:139-189), but the finding's fit argument fails on both prongs. (a) "Does not appear in the task plan": the task's own lessons file records every one of these as review follow-ups of this same fix — the object-literal-lookup-is-not-closed → use a Map rule (lessons:57-59), the "OOXML attribute only through a converter that can fail closed" rule that produces listLevelAttr (lessons:45-53), and the dropped API-side alignment allowlist replaced by writer normalization, i.e. the backend serializeBlockStyle/parseBlockStyle rewrite (lessons:60-65, mirrored by the controller comment at docs-content.controller.ts:265-270). (b) Rubric: the two OOXML files are the exact sinks the plan already required touching (todo:47-53, 64-72) and the hardening lands in the same functions; no stated Non-Goal is exceeded (Non-goals are palette/picker UI, highlight path, no migration — todo:108-113) and the sole acceptance criterion (todo:104) is unaffected. The stated harm is review/revert ergonomics, which this lens classifies as a preference (minor), and minor never blocks.

finding.summary: Block-style serializer is duplicated backend/frontend; only the backend copy was hardened, so the two CRDT encoders now diverge
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` were changed to emit only present/finite fields and to ignore non-finite attributes, but the near-identical copy in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-227 still does `alignment: style.alignment` / `String(style.lineHeight)` unconditionally and `Number(attrs.x)` without a finite check. Both write and read the same Yorkie Tree, so the same document is now encoded/decoded by two different rule sets — the repo's reuse expectation would put this logic in one shared module instead.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. Backend docs-tree.ts:139-189 has the hardened serializer/parser (present-and-finite emission, non-finite attributes ignored, with an explanatory comment). The frontend copy at yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-215 still emits `alignment: style.alignment` and `String(style.lineHeight)`/`String(style.marginTop)`… unconditionally, and :217-227 parses with `Number(attrs.x)` behind only an `in attrs` presence check with no finite guard. There is no downstream guard: packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274 shows `normalizeBlockStyle` is a bare `{ ...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style }` spread that preserves NaN. Both encoders target the same Yorkie `content` Tree — backend via docs-content.controller.ts:102/164 (readDocsRoot/writeDocsRoot), frontend via yorkie-doc-store.ts:588-595 and buildBlockNode:332-366 — so one document is now encoded/decoded by two different rule sets. The duplication is real and self-acknowledged in the backend file header (docs-tree.ts:1-22), which itself prescribes extracting the shared helper into `@wafflebase/docs` (the package both copies already import DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE/normalizeBlockStyle from), and docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:163-168 documents the same mirror coupling. That is a duplication/reuse fit violation in this lens, not a line-level nit, so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: Design doc claims the shared `toRgbHexColor` normalizes `<a:srgbClr val>` in `color.ts`, but the implementation only normalizes at the two call sites in `export/pptx/text.ts`
finding.evidence: The doc edit is placed under the "**Colors (`color.ts`)**" bullet: "`{ kind: 'srgb', hex }` → `<a:srgbClr val="RRGGBB">`, where the hex is first normalized by the shared `toRgbHexColor`". But `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35` is untouched and still does `escapeXmlAttr(c.value.replace(/^#/, '').toUpperCase())`. Every other srgbClr sink that flows through `colorChildXml`/`solidFillXml`/`gradFillXml` (shape fills, gradient stops, shadow colors, `theme.ts:84` clrScheme) therefore still emits whatever string the model holds. The doc describes a sink-level invariant that the change implements only at the caller level for run/marker text, so the normalization is at the wrong layer and the doc overstates the guarantee.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim does not hold. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts` is NOT untouched and does not do `escapeXmlAttr(c.value.replace(/^#/, '').toUpperCase())`: it imports `toRgbHexColor` from `@wafflebase/docs` (color.ts:1) and normalizes inside `colorChildXml` itself at color.ts:42 (`const hex = toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000'`), with an explanatory comment at color.ts:35-41 saying this is the backstop for mandatory sinks. Because `solidFillXml` (color.ts:46-48), `gradFillXml` (color.ts:56-66) and `fillXml` (color.ts:74-77) all route through `colorChildXml`, shape fills, gradient stops and background/shadow fills are normalized at the sink level — the opposite of what the finding asserts. The design doc also does not overstate: docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md:151-167 explicitly splits "Omittable sinks (`text.ts` … normalize before building the `ThemeColor`, in `storedColorToThemeColor`)" from "Mandatory sinks … normalize inside `colorChildXml` itself and fall back to `000000`", which matches the implementation (text.ts:188, 208). The only path not routed through `toRgbHexColor` is `theme.ts:83`'s `toSrgbHex` for `clrScheme`, which the doc describes in a separate `theme.ts` section (theme.ts:71-73) and never claims goes through `color.ts`; that is a different (at most minor/taste) observation, not the doc-vs-code contradiction alleged here.

finding.summary: Alignment hardening (backend PUT validation + `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` closed map) is unrelated to the originating color-reset issue (#728) — unrequested scope creep
finding.evidence: Every other hunk in the change is traceable to #728 (empty-string reset color: `resolveStoredColor`, `toRgbHexColor`, the picker passing `undefined`, cell-style attribute removal). `assertValidBlockStyle` in the backend controller and `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` in `docs-style-map.ts` validate `style.alignment`, which no path in #728 touches. It is a separate concern (OOXML attribute injection via alignment) bundled into a rendering/data-model bug fix, with a new API-level 400 behavior that is not recorded in `docs/design/rest-api.md`.

verdict.reason: The finding's central artifact does not exist. There is no `assertValidBlockStyle` anywhere in source (repo-wide grep hits only `.agent-review/*` reviewer artifacts), and the backend controller performs no alignment validation at all: `assertValidBlock` (docs-content.controller.ts:254-312) checks only `typeof b.style === 'object'` and carries an explicit comment (`:265-273`) stating that style *values* are intentionally NOT constrained because "every OOXML sink resolves `alignment` through its own closed lookup". A grep for `alignment` across packages/backend/src returns only test fixtures, the pre-existing docs-tree attr round-trip, and that comment. So there is no new API-level 400 for alignment, which also voids the derived `docs/design/rest-api.md` gap claim. The second artifact is misnamed (`docs-style-map.ts` does not exist); `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is at packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:118-123 and is present, but it is recorded in the canonical subsystem design doc docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md:436-439 inside the same "export fails closed" converter table whose preamble (:428-434) explicitly cites issue #728's `''` reset color alongside `toRgbHexColor`/`toDocxHexColor` — i.e. same sink policy, same section, canonical doc, not a parallel doc and not an unrecorded design change. The compound presence claim therefore fails on its named location and on its design-doc premise.

finding.summary: Cell-style clear semantics changed but the canonical tables design doc was not updated (still shows `backgroundColor=""` as a stored cell attribute)
finding.evidence: This delta adds `removedCellStyleAttrs` + `removeStyleByPath` to `applyCellStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:249,2432), establishing the convention that a cleared cell attribute is REMOVED from the Yorkie cell node rather than merged over with an empty value. The canonical subsystem doc `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md` — the doc that specifies the cell node attribute set (lines 156-166) and shows the tree shape — still depicts `cell(backgroundColor="" …)` at line 138 and describes `backgroundColor` simply as "CSS color string" with no mention that clearing removes the attribute. Two design docs WERE updated in this PR (docs-docx-import-export.md, slides-pptx-export.md), so the omission is specific to the table cell-style contract this delta actually changes.

verdict.reason: The canonical doc WAS updated with exactly the contract the finding says is absent. docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md:171-177 adds a "Clearing a cell attribute" section stating that an absent attribute means "unset", that "there is no empty-string form of a cell style", that clearing (the "No fill" reset of issue #728) must REMOVE the attribute because "styleByPath only merges", and that storing "" would push a value every paint/export path must special-case into the CRDT. Lines 179-188 further document the node-scoping hazard of removeStyleByPath(cellPath, cellPath+1), the [idx, idx+1) opening-tag range workaround, the helper removeCellNodeStyle in yorkie-doc-store.ts, and that applyCellStyle and applyCellSpan both route through it. The finding's quoted evidence is also wrong on its face: line 138 reads cell(backgroundColor="#fff2cc" verticalAlign="top" padding="4"), not backgroundColor="". The doc tracks the shipped code: yorkie-doc-store.ts:255-261 (removedCellStyleAttrs, explicitly mirroring removedInlineStyleAttrs) and :277-285 (removeCellNodeStyle via pathToIndex + removeStyle(from, from+1)), called at :2472 (applyCellStyle) and :2522 (applyCellSpan). The updated text sits at lines 171-188, just past the 125-170 window the reviewer read, and a grep for removeStyleByPath under docs/design does return docs-tables.md:179.
